detail: An operator reclaim over a 10k-post store is answered 'uncertain operator reclaim' (CLI exit 3) while the owner's pass is still running and later completes. Mechanism (lane n-g27-reds-2, 2026-10-08, train-27 developer image, run hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/n-row36/native-g27reds2-d, test_native_reclaim_walk test_resident_set_of_a_pass_at_1k_and_10k with FN_RUN_RECLAIM_RSS=1): fnn-control-exchange (host/native/control-transport.lisp:225) waits fn-nco-reply-seconds for the reply = *fn-nco-reply-grace-seconds* 10 s (books/control-observation.lisp:3-9) plus 1 s per 64 KiB of REQUEST octets. The owner logged 'RECLAIM request ... answer=requested' and 'CHECKPOINT release ... held=pending' (the auto checkpoint alone took ms=11918) and no pass end before the client gave up. At 1k the pass takes 1.55 s and fits. The deadline scales with the request's size, not with the work the request asks for, so any control verb whose work grows with the store (reclaim, a publication, a checkpoint) turns 'uncertain' past ~10 s: a fixed ceiling on store-sized work (D27). The client's 'uncertain' is honest; the defect is that the deadline is not the request's own bound. Fix shapes (decision owed): (a) ACL2 computes the reply deadline from the verb's declared work bound for this store (the quanta the pass may take x the quantum bound), so the client waits for what the owner promised; or (b) store-sized verbs answer at :requested with a receipt and the client observes completion through status (no deadline on the work, only on the acknowledgement). Then the 10k reclaim RSS test's exit-3 expectation is restored to exit 0.
notes: 2026-10-08 (coordinator, via N): fix (b). Store-sized verbs (reclaim, publication, checkpoint) answer :requested with a receipt at once; the client observes completion through status; the reply deadline applies only to the acknowledgement (as BP and publication already behave). Books decide which verbs are store-sized: a declared class on the verb, not a size heuristic. Keystone: a :requested receipt is followed by exactly one completion status. Owner C (control transport). Then restore test_resident_set_of_a_pass_at_1k_and_10k's 10k reclaim to exit 0.

S1 (control-receipt): Every control verb (FNCT kind, and the declared verb within an administrative kind) is declared :bounded (work bounded by the request; the reply deadline applies) or :store-sized (answers :requested with a receipt). The declaration is total over the kind table, checked by evaluation.
S2 (control-receipt): An admitted :store-sized verb replies :requested with a receipt, never its completion, and never waits on its work: the owner answers in the quantum accepting the request.

S3 (control-receipt, keystone): For every receipt the owner issues there is exactly one completion status observed through status: its state goes :requested to exactly one terminal word, never back and never twice. State this over the owner step the host calls, with a positive witness of the whole antecedent and conclusion and a hypothesis-removal witness refusing a second completion. Eventual completion requires the owner to continue executing and receive a work outcome; process death and recovery must retain an honest unresolved outcome.

S4 (control-receipt): The client reply deadline covers only the acknowledgement for :store-sized verbs. Subsequent status observation uses an ACL2-named wait policy bounding each observation, with no fixed ceiling on store-sized work.

2026-10-08 (control-receipt implementation, uncommitted): The shared FNCT kind/verb declaration now drives native-control-kinds, native-admin plans and work classification. Kinds 3/17 classify declared reclaim request/recorded/dry-run and compaction request as store-sized; other verbs and every other kind 1..25 are bounded. In particular identity 24/25 and consumer 4/5/9/6 remain bounded. Publication/checkpoint use the compaction request producer.

Owner acceptance issues a process-local epoch/serial receipt and sends the reasoned requested acknowledgement before invoking the existing producer. One outstanding maintenance slot retains its terminal outcome until explicit release; status reads preserve it. The CLI prints the receipt, observes status with fn-nco-wait-seconds (1/10 second), and has no total work deadline. Unknown receipts remain uncertain, and lost acknowledgement recovery prints the held receipt on the next maintenance request. Producer persistence uncertainty fences the owner and retains an uncertain terminal result.

Proof scope: fn-nco-owner-step is the actual host entry. Exactly-once safety, matching terminal-observation progress, state preservation, serial freshness, stale-completion refusal and status observation are admitted; unconditional producer termination or persistence across process death is not proved. The source-projected proof_repl session control-receipt-final-3 admitted every new theorem plus the exact defteeth claim, positive witness, all three hypothesis-removal witnesses and duplicate-completion mutation. It loaded all 144 source forms (stopped_at null; final FN-REPL-DONE 145). The sandbox then denied the REPL UNIX control socket (EPERM), so this is admission evidence, not a live REPL or certification claim. Projection uses unchanged dependency/source events, no axioms or stubs.

Validation: tests.test_control_observation exercises actual handler/client/compaction functions with deterministic I/O seams, including acknowledgement-before-work, a 20-second outcome exceeding the 11-second request deadline, lost acknowledgement recovery, repeat status, duplicate completion refusal and stale publication deferral. The 1k/10k native reclaim RSS test explicitly requires exit 0 and a printed receipt. Native execution and affected certification remain pending; certify_books --jobs 2 --affected-by books/control-observation.lisp selects 127 books, too large for the requested small laptop closure. No image build, commit or push was performed.

Final local gates (control-receipt): lock_discipline_check has 271 findings and 66 baseline-new keys, exactly as origin/dev (0 added, 0 removed; stderr empty); host_check --read: 0 unreadable files; interface_emit --check: 0 class/kind disagreements, all 1795 dispatched entries declared, sole finding stale generated planning/interfaces.json; tests.test_control_observation: 2 tests OK; secrets_check: 15 files, 0 findings; git diff --check clean. BSD grep rejects -P, so an equivalent Python scan checked all changed files and found 0 non-ASCII lines. Coordinator natives: tests.test_native_control, tests.test_native_admin, tests.test_native_operator_cli, tests.test_native_checkpoint_auto, tests.test_native_maintenance_live, tests.test_native_log_compaction, tests.test_native_reclaim_in_flight, tests.test_native_reclaim_walk (FN_RUN_RECLAIM_RSS=1).

S3a (C8, statement first): Over the actual fn-nco-owner-step, in every reachable owner state each requested receipt has exactly one pending producer job naming it, and every pending producer job names exactly one requested receipt. Acceptance creates both atomically; only that job's terminal outcome leaves requested and consumes the job, mapping to exactly one terminal status. The host executes the job held by that state, not an untracked copy of its request.

S3b (C8, statement first): Over fn-nco-wire-step, the status entry the host calls, a status query for a receipt the owner does not hold (after death/restart or for an unissued serial) answers the distinct word receipt-unknown, never requested and never a terminal word. The ACL2 client decision maps receipt-unknown to uncertain, exit 3, and stops polling. Persistence across process death is not claimed beyond this observation contract.

C8 product defect found: round 1 had no pending producer job in the owner state; the request argv/token lived only in host locals. The step could not establish the requested-receipt/job correspondence. Add the producer job to the existing receipt state and make the worker read that held job. Prove initial reachability, step preservation, the bijection and outcome-only removal, with statement-bound teeth; prove unknown-receipt status and CLI consequences with teeth.

C8 result: fn-nco-owner-step now atomically stores the requested receipt and its single (receipt argv) job in the same state. The worker reads fn-nco-pending-job from that state. fn-nco-initial-has-no-orphan, fn-nco-owner-step-has-no-orphan, fn-nco-owner-run-has-no-orphan and fn-nco-reachable-receipts-have-one-job prove the requested-receipt/job bijection for every reachable state; fn-nco-only-job-outcome-leaves-requested proves outcome-only removal. Existing exactly-once completion and retained-status laws still hold. The positive witnesses are reachable accepted requests; removal/mutation witnesses expose a dropped job, a job left after completion, duplicate completion, a restarted owner promising work and indefinite polling of an unknown receipt.

C8 S3b: fn-nco-unknown-receipt-status proves the actual fn-nco-wire-step returns the distinct receipt-unknown word for any token it does not hold; fn-nco-unknown-receipt-stops-with-exit-3 proves the client decision returns uncertain, stops polling and maps through the shared fn-wide exit classifier to 3. The host uses that decision for both initial/manual replies and polling. A deterministic test restarts the owner after ACK and asserts exactly two exchanges (ACK and unknown status), exit 3 and no release. An unissued serial is tested separately. Persistence across process death is not claimed beyond S3b.

title: a store-sized control verb (reclaim at 10k) is answered uncertain after a fixed 10 s reply grace that scales with request octets, not with the verb's work
